clue.text: I'm obsequious, but I refuse to accept bad copy

indicators.note: one piece accepting another takes it inside, so the refusal is opened up to hold the rest

parts.note: a curt 'I refuse' is SHAN'T, short for shall not

indicators.note: bad copy is spoilt, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fawning person protests they won't take on a poorly written text.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken in the first person, as the toady might describe himself; 'I refuse' as a single word is the contraction of shall not.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady speaking of himself would admit to fawning servility, which is what this flatterer embodies.

clue.text: Not so hairy as a ferret? Not entirely

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters lie within it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether something is less frightening than a ferret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairy' looks like furry, as a ferret is; it is slang for frightening or risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is slang for dangerous, so less hairy means less risky.

clue.text: Plot to recycle old clue

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter schemes to reuse a stale crossword clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To collude is to conspire secretly, a synonym for the verb plot.

clue.text: One affirming faith? That's academic

definitions.meaning: one who professes a belief openly declares it
a senior university teacher holds this title

explanation.surface: A believer declares their faith, but it doesn't matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who professes a religion declares it, and a senior university teacher bears the same title.

clue.text: Conceal tiny changes in weather system

explanation.surface: Hide small variations in the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticyclone is a high-pressure weather system bringing settled conditions.

clue.text: Member of orchestra shortly to have bath

indicators.note: said shortly, the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: the tuba is a brass instrument in an orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestral player will soon take a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is an informal word for a bathtub.

clue.text: An apostle's pronounced shock

indicators.note: said out loud, so the phrase is replaced by a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; Paul is the apostle who wrote the epistles

explanation.surface: Something an apostle once said caused offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An apostle' is A PAUL, which spoken runs together into the verb meaning dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to fill them with horror, so it is a synonym for the verb shock.

clue.text: Friend! May I proceed?

definitions.meaning: a Spanish word for pal used in English
read as '...?', asking whether one is cleared to go ahead

explanation.surface: A greeting to a pal, followed by a request to continue.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend and is used familiarly in English, often as a form of address.

clue.text: Quietly discussing outcome of cup draw

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical instruction to play quietly
airing views is discussing them openly

explanation.surface: Fans talk in hushed tones about the result of the cup draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup draw decides which teams meet, so its result is a set of matches between pairs.

clue.text: In general, the French destiny's still hidden

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

indicators.note: the second piece is concealed inside the first

parts.note: fate is destiny
yet means still, as in 'not finished yet'

explanation.surface: In general, the destiny of the French remains unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'generally speaking', but general is the definition: the French marquis who served in the American Revolutionary War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquis de Lafayette was a French general who fought in the American Revolutionary War.

clue.text: Collapse when I knocked out hooligan in quarrel

indicators.note: a letter knocked out of a word is removed from it

parts.note: to collapse, as a business might, is to fail
taken as written
a lout is a rowdy, uncouth young man

explanation.surface: Someone collapses after being punched during a fight with a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collapse' looks like the definition with 'fall'; it is FAIL, which loses its I. 'when' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-out is a disagreement between friends, a synonym for a quarrel.

clue.text: In blow, decline to be officer

indicators.note: the second piece goes in the first, as 'in blow' places the decline inside the punch

parts.note: a biff is a punch or blow
to ail is to decline in health

explanation.surface: A man's punch weakens before he becomes a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is a court official, an officer who enforces orders such as evictions.

clue.text: Plane finally on flight path

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: a rout is a disorderly retreat, a flight from battle

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An aircraft at last sets off on its flight path.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a course or way taken, a synonym for path.

clue.text: Killer of pet? That's a strange thing

definitions.meaning: the proverb says ... killed the cat, a household pet

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what killed their pet, finding it all very peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names inquisitiveness as a cat's killer, and an oddity or rare object is also called by this word.

clue.text: Ordinary people controlled by the castle

definitions.meaning: the ordinary members of a group
in chess the castle, or rook, moves along rows and columns

explanation.surface: The common folk are ruled by the lord in his fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The castle is the chess rook, which commands the rows (ranks) and columns (files) of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary members of a group, as distinct from leaders, are called this, and in chess the rows and columns are also so named.

clue.text: Fear of a 7 on board

parts.note: seven-down is a pairing; at the bridge table West and East form one partnership

explanation.surface: Dread of being drawn as a pair at the games table.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 refers to 7-down, PAIRING. In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, and West-East sit as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential dread, a synonym for fear in its sense of wonder mixed with fright.

clue.text: A TV programme best to avoid extremes, however

parts.note: a sitcom is a television situation comedy

indicators.note: avoiding the extremes of a word drops its first and last letters, keeping the middle

explanation.surface: Advice that a television show should steer clear of excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking things as they come means accepting them however they happen, so the phrase matches however.

clue.text: Something uncanny not visited at very start of tour?

definitions.text: Something uncanny not visited at very start of tour?

parts.words: Something uncanny not visited at very start of tour?
parts.note: a tourist skipping the first attraction sees the next one on the list; also the uncanny gift of foreseeing events

explanation.surface: A sightseeing trip omits its first stop, which seems eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyance, the supposed power of perceiving future events, is called by this name and is uncanny.

clue.text: With humbug, speech appears flatter

parts.note: a humbug is a striped British boiled mint sweet
talk is speech

explanation.surface: Speech full of nonsense seems duller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like 'more flat'; it is the verb to compliment. A humbug is a British peppermint sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweet-talk someone is to coax them with compliments, a synonym for flatter.

clue.text: Multinational force worried, being put in the middle

parts.note: Interpol is the international police organisation
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: An international police body is anxious about being caught in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpolate is to insert something between other things, such as words into a text.

clue.text: Dismiss parade

definitions.meaning: to turn someone out is to expel or dismiss them
a military ... is a parade or muster of troops

explanation.surface: A sergeant dismisses the parade.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out someone is to eject them, and a turnout is a muster, as on a parade ground.

clue.text: Failure to win may make one hot under the collar

definitions.meaning: a drawn match, with neither side winning

definitions.text: may make one hot under the collar
definitions.meaning: a neckband knotted beneath the shirt collar can make one warm

explanation.surface: Not winning can leave a player angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn result is called this, and so is the neckwear knotted under a shirt collar.

clue.text: Foot — gosh! — trapped in oak

indicators.note: one piece trapped in another lies inside it

parts.note: an oak is a tree
och is a Scottish exclamation like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims after getting their foot stuck in an oak.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochee is a metrical foot of one stressed syllable followed by an unstressed one.

clue.text: Lover and lass here in spring end frolic with a tumble

definitions.text: Lover and lass here in spring

indicators.note: letters given a tumble fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Young lovers in springtime end their romp by falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the Shakespeare song 'It was a lover and his lass', who passed 'o'er the green cornfield' in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song from As You Like It the lovers pass over a field of grain in spring, so this is where they are.

clue.text: Fine, delicate sort of story?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
airy means light and delicate

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a story is fine and light.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy story is a kind of tale, and the word also hints at a far-fetched lie.

clue.text: Seeing nothing in children, but he had a Nipper

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: tots are small children
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Seeing nothing among the kids, though one father had a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' looks like a child; it is Susan Nipper of Dickens's Dombey and Son, whom Mr Toots married.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dombey and Son the amiable Mr Toots ends up married to the maid Susan Nipper.

clue.text: Small spot in which plan announced

indicators.note: said aloud, the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a spec, short for specification, is a detailed plan

explanation.surface: A small place where a scheme was unveiled.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck is a tiny spot or particle.

clue.text: Making fast call from Jersey by phone

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of cow, whose call is a moo
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: Quickly ringing someone on the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like the Channel Island; it is the dairy cow breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring a boat is securing it with ropes, which sailors call making it fast.

clue.text: Pick up sack — a gift of it?

indicators.note: in a down answer, picking up reads the word upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: Lift the sack: is there a present inside?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition relies on the idiom 'the gift of the gab', a talent for fluent talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'gift of the gab' means a talent for persuasive chatter, so this is what the gift is of.

clue.text: A Russian garden, one Rowena loved

parts.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name
to hoe is to work in a garden

explanation.surface: A Russian man's garden, belonging to a woman's beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scott's novel the Saxon heroine Rowena loves the knight who gives the book its title.

clue.text: Pause to eat a spicy dish

indicators.note: one piece eating another takes it inside

parts.note: to stay is to pause or remain

explanation.surface: Someone stops to have a hot meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a Southeast Asian dish of skewered meat with spicy peanut sauce.

clue.text: Ketch's objective, such speed?

definitions.meaning: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English hangman, whose aim was to snap the victim's neck
dangerously fast, as in a headlong pace

explanation.surface: A sailing boat's goal is to go very fast.
explanation.walkthrough: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat, but here Ketch is the hangman Jack Ketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman aims to snap the neck, and a reckless pace that could cause such a fatal injury is described the same way.
